title: Using Magnetometry to Monitor Cellular Incorporation and Subsequent Biodegradation of Chemically Synthetized Iron Oxide Nanoparticles
protocol: Dissolve 400 mg of iron(III) acetylacetonate in 10 mL of benzyl alcohol within a 30 mL monowave glass vial.
Increase the temperature of the suspension from 25 to 250 °C in 20 min and maintain it at 250 °C for 30 min using a microwave reactor.
Transfer the resulting nanoparticles suspended in benzyl alcohol to a glass vial.
Separate the nanoparticles using a neodymium magnet for 30 min.
Wash the precipitate with 10 mL of dichloromethane, then with 1 M sodium hydroxide, followed by ethanol and pH 7 water (three times) using a neodymium magnet for 5 min each step.
Adjust the nanoparticle suspension in water to pH 2 using 1 M hydrochloric acid.
Centrifuge the suspension in 100 kDa ultracentrifugal filters at 2,200 x g for 10 min and remove the filtrate.
Add 12 mL of 10-2 M hydrochloric acid to the nanoparticles solution and centrifuge in 100 kDa ultracentrifugal filters at 2,200 x g for 10 min (three times).
Dilute the nanoparticles solution within 10 mL of 10-2 M hydrochloric acid before coating.
Dilute 175 mg of citric acid and polyacrylic acid in water at pH 2 in a 100 mL glass vial.
Add 10 mL of nanoparticles aqueous dispersion to the coating molecule solution at a mass ratio of 5 between the coating molecule and the nanoparticles.
Agitate for 2 hours under magnetic stirring at room temperature.
Adjust the pH to 7 with 1 M sodium hydroxide after agitation.
Centrifuge the nanoparticle solution 3 times with deionized (DI) water in 100 kDa ultracentrifugal filters at 2,200 x g for 10 minutes.
Remove the filtrate and dilute the nanoparticles solution in 12 mL of DI water.
Culture human mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) in complete Mesenchymal Stem Cell Growth Medium (MSCGM) at 37 °C and 5% CO₂.
When the cells reach 90% confluence, add 10 mL of pre-warmed trypsin-EDTA at 37°C per 150 cm² flask.
Leave for 2 to 3 minutes to detach the cells.
Observe the detached cells with a bright-field microscope.
Resuspend the detached cells in MSCGM and divide them into four 150 cm² flasks.
Amplify the cells until passage 4 to 5.

Prepare the solution of magnetic nanoparticles for cell labeling by dispersing the chosen concentration of iron oxide nanoparticles in serum-free Roswell Park Memorial Institute (RPMI-1640) medium without glutamine.
When the cells are at passage 4 or 5 and 90% confluent, remove MSCGM medium.
Rinse the cells with serum-free RPMI without glutamine.
Add 10 mL of iron oxide nanoparticles solution per 150 cm2 culture flask to cover all the cells.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Discard the nanoparticle solution.
Wash once with serum-free RPMI-1640 without glutamine.
Incubate with DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin (25 mL per 150 cm2 flask) overnight at 37 °C and 5% CO2 to allow complete internalization of the nanoparticles.

Freshly prepare cell-spheroid culture medium composed of DMEM high glucose with L-glutamine supplemented with 50 µM L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate, 0.1 µM dexamethasone, 1 mM sodium pyruvate, 0.35 mM L-proline, and 1% universal culture supplement.
Detach the magnetic MSCs by adding 10 mL of 0.05% trypsin-EDTA pre-warmed at 37 °C per 150 cm2 flask for 2-3 minutes.
Inactivate the trypsin immediately by adding 1/3 volume of DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin pre-warmed at 37 °C.
Centrifuge the dissociated cells at 260 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the media from the cells.
Re-suspend the cells in less than 1 mL of cell-spheroid culture medium per 150 cm² flask.
Count the cell number using a hemocytometer.
Adjust the volume if needed to contain approximately 200,000 cells in about 50 µL of medium.
Add 1 mL of freshly prepared cell-spheroid culture medium to a sterile conical centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the magnetically labeled cells at 180 x g for 3 min.
Keep the supernatant as the cell culture medium.
Slightly open the tubes to allow air exchange.
Incubate the tubes at 37 °C with 5% CO2 for up to 21 days.
Change the medium twice a week during the incubation period.
Wash the spheroids twice with cacodylate buffer on given days.
Fix the spheroids using 2% glutaraldehyde in 0.1 M cacodylate buffer for 30 min at room temperature.
Store the fixed spheroids in PBS until used for VSM measurement or TEM imaging.
Place up to 10 µL of magnetic nanoparticle solution or a single cell-spheroid into the sample holder designed for VSM.
Insert the sample into the VSM and scan for sample offset.
Position the sample at the magnetization maximum.
Perform the first measurement with a low magnetic field between -1500 Oe and +1500 Oe, at a rate of 20 Oe/s.
Perform the second measurement with a high magnetic field between -30 000 Oe and +30 000 Oe, at a rate of 200 Oe/s.
Deposit 10 μL of aqueous nanoparticle solution onto a carbon-coated copper grid for TEM analysis.
Allow the deposited solution to dry at room temperature.
Contrast fixed cell-spheroids containing nanoparticles with 0.5% Oolong Tea Extract (OTE) diluted in 0.1 M cacodylate buffer.
Post-fix treated samples with 1% osmium tetroxide containing 1.5% potassium cyanoferrate.
Dehydrate the samples through graded ethanol baths before embedding them in Epon.
Slice ultrathin sections of 70 nm and deposit onto cooper grids for TEM analysis.
Capture images using an electron microscope at 80 kV, with magnifications ranging from 1k to observe entire cells to 40k to examine endosomal compartments.
